bugs.error_message: VSCode: 'The Python path in your debug configuration is invalid.' for the service-ai debug config (.venv/bin/python)
bugs.root_cause: services/service-ai/.venv/bin/python is a symlink chain: python -> python3.13 -> /opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.13/bin/python3.13. The Homebrew python@3.13 formula was uninstalled/upgraded off the system at some point, so the final symlink target no longer exists — the venv's own pyvenv.cfg still referenced the old backend/services/service-ai/.venv path from before the monorepo migration too, confirming the venv predates several changes and was never recreated.
bugs.fix: Deleted and recreated the venv with the system's working python3.13 (~/.local/bin/python3.13, 3.13.12) via `python3.13 -m venv .venv`, then reinstalled from requirements.txt. Verified: imports work (fastapi/uvicorn/httpx) and the service's own pytest suite passes (10/10).

bugs.error_message: [ioredis] Unhandled error event: ReplyError: ERR Can't execute 'info': only (P|S)SUBSCRIBE / (P|S)UNSUBSCRIBE / PING / QUIT / RESET are allowed in this context — logged right after 'Redis reconnect attempt #1'
bugs.root_cause: All three services create a dedicated pub/sub Redis connection via datasources.coreRedis.duplicate() and immediately call psubscribe/subscribe on it, putting that connection into Redis subscribe-mode (server-side, only (P|S)SUBSCRIBE/UNSUBSCRIBE/PING/QUIT/RESET are legal from then on). ioredis defaults to enableReadyCheck:true, which runs an internal INFO command on every (re)connection to verify the server is ready before marking the connection 'ready'. On a reconnect (network blip, redis restart, or in this investigation a deliberate CLIENT KILL to force one), ioredis re-issues that INFO check on the subscribe-mode connection, Redis rejects it per protocol, and ioredis surfaces it as an unhandled error event plus a retry loop — even though the subscription itself is still functioning after reconnect.
bugs.fix: Pass { enableReadyCheck: false } as the duplicate() override on all three subscribe-only connections (ioredis's own documented workaround for this exact issue — see the wiki link in ioredis's own ready-check warning message). Verified end-to-end: booted all three services, force-killed their subscribe connections at the Redis server via CLIENT KILL to trigger a real reconnect (confirmed via the 'Redis reconnect attempt #1' log line), and confirmed zero 'Unhandled error event'/INFO errors afterward — previously this exact sequence reproduced the bug every time.

bugs.error_message: User: kartları çevir diyince kartlar aşağı kayıyor
bugs.root_cause: Two distinct issues, verified separately with a Playwright-driven real browser against the live signal-engine: (1) minor: SignalCard's flipped BACK face used position:absolute without top/left, so its containing-block offset defaulted to the in-flow static position instead of the relative FRONT face's top-left corner — cosmetically wrong but not the reported symptom, since BACK content never exceeded FRONT's height in practice. (2) actual root cause: SignalGrid's default sort is by confluenceScore, and the bot emits a new signal every few seconds; each new signal re-sorts the ENTIRE visible list. Clicking 'Çevir' does nothing to the sort, but because the grid keeps re-sorting live in the background, the card the user just flipped (and its neighbors) visually jump to new positions within ~600ms-3s, making it look like flipping itself causes the shift. Verified via instrumented Playwright script: card identities at the same grid index changed completely within 600ms of a flip with zero interaction, purely from live signal arrivals.
bugs.fix: (1) Added top:0, left:0 to the BACK face's absolute positioning (correctness fix, low impact in practice). (2) Real fix: SignalGrid now tracks a flippedIds Set (via a new onFlipChange callback prop threaded through SignalCard) and freezes the visible sort order in a ref while any card is flipped — new signals still appear (appended at the end, not spliced into their score-sorted position) but no existing card's position changes until the user flips the card back closed. Verified end-to-end with a live signal-engine + market-data + vite dev server under Playwright: card order was byte-identical before and 3 seconds into a flip (during which the bot emitted multiple new signals), and resumed normal live sorting immediately after un-flipping.

bugs.error_message: would have thrown ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for '../service-signal-engine/src/{indicators,liquidation-pressure,confluence,setup-builder}.js' once those files moved to core/
bugs.root_cause: Same anti-pattern as bug-tracker-broken-import: service-backtest's main.js imported four signal-engine domain modules via relative cross-service paths ('../service-signal-engine/src/...'). This would have broken (or already had, depending on migration ordering) once service-signal-engine's domain files moved into core/service-signal-engine/src/domain/.

bugs.error_message: ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find module '.../service-signal-engine/src/signal-repository.js' imported from services/service-tracker/main.js
bugs.root_cause: service-tracker discovered a real pre-existing bug: main.js imported getPendingOutcomes/resolveOutcome via a relative cross-service path '../service-signal-engine/src/signal-repository.js'. This broke the moment service-signal-engine's signal-repository.js moved to core/ during the monorepo migration (clean-architecture split), but the underlying anti-pattern (one service reaching into another service's internal src/ via relative import) was already fragile before the migration.
bugs.fix: Refactored to composition-root pattern: services/service-tracker/src/container.js now imports makeSignalRepository from the shared @borsa-bot/core-signal-engine workspace package and wires it via dependency injection, instead of any relative cross-service import.

Muhasebe tarafi (evaluateSimOutcome/getSignalStats) 2*0.0006 + kayma = ~0.0018 kullaniyordu. Yani kapinin gecirdigi bazi setup'lar muhasebede zarar yaziyordu; kapi ile olcum ayni maliyeti gormuyordu.
bugs.fix: buildSetup'a feeRoundtrip parametresi eklendi (varsayilan 0.0008 = geriye uyumlu). boot.js artik 2*takerFee + slippagePct + exitSlippagePct formuluyle bot_config'ten hesaplayip geciriyor; run-strategy.js backtest tarafinda AYNI formulu kullaniyor (parite). bugs.error_message: Karar metriginin (avg_sim_r) hicbir yerde hata payi yoktu — Wilson SADECE win_rate'e uygulaniyordu

StatsPage'e karar metrigi paneli eklendi: provenPositive=false iken sari uyari 'edge HENUZ kanitlanmadi'. Olculen: n=110'da CI=[-0.161,+0.235] -> kanitlanmadi; kanit icin ~3160 islem (~63 gun) gerekiyor.

bugs.error_message: $6 teminat / 10x kaldirac ~%20 iflas riski tasiyor — bu hesap onceki oturumda 'yapilmali' denip hic yapilmamisti

Monte Carlo (20k tur): iflas orani ~%20, medyan +$44 ama %5 senaryo $0. Ayrica $6/10x karari mum-kirliligi bulgusundan ONCE alinmisti, dayandigi win-rate tahminleri artik gecersiz.
bugs.fix: HENUZ UYGULANMADI — plana yazildi. Kaldirac taramasi: iflas riski sermayeden degil KALDIRACtan geliyor (10x her hesap boyutunda ~%20, 3x'te %0.3). Oneri 10x -> 3x. Faz 3 karar kapisina 'pozisyon boyutu iflas riski <%2' maddesi eklendi.
